C-RECORD-PARSE.Summary: Convert the record engine from regex-over-XML to parse-and-splice. scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts today reads record structure one way (six parser calls) and rewrites it another (seven built regexes, ten string .replace() call expressions, seven of them document mutations — counts re-measured at 49b4ebb; see Assumptions), and nothing keeps the two views in agreement. This bundle adds a parser-derived source-span capability to the shared XML adapter (src/artifact/xml.ts, M-GRAMMAR), converts every structural read in the engine to the parsed tree, converts every structural write to a byte-preserving splice positioned by parser-derived spans, ships the minimal shape check that makes span pairing well defined, and removes the archived-spec prose pass from derivePayerMap so that payment is declared structurally (registry rows) rather than sniffed out of spec sentences. The two discriminating probes the authority built — the false-payment fixture and the XML equivalence-class variants — are inherited as acceptance criteria and as tests. Name re-searched at this commit (49b4ebb): 76 archive directories and 0 registry rows in either layer carry the name or the tokens PARSE, PARSER, ENGINE, MATCH, SHAPE.
C-RECORD-PARSE.Problem:
The record engine matches XML with regexes instead of parsing it, and the two views disagree under legal XML variation. Staged finding F209 (.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md, not yet in the record) measured the engine at c920415: six parseGraceXmlArtifact calls beside seven constructed regexes and string-replacement mutations, with attrOf reading an attribute from anywhere inside an element's text rather than its open tag, and withStatusRetired rewriting the first status occurrence rather than the open tag's. Re-measured at 49b4ebb for this spec: the same inventory holds, and the equivalence-class probe below reproduces the disagreement against the live record.
This is one defect wearing four hats, each staged, not yet in the record: F209 (regex over XML is unsound under legal variation), F208 (a spec that quotes the payer phrase pays by accident — a false payment), F207 (no shape check: the record's structure is convention, so structural reasoning counts something undefined), and F206 (volume is measured in file lines, so formatting moves the budget). The engine's own regex path and its parser path were observed to disagree by one live element on two of three legal rewrites of a single open tag, measured for this spec at 49b4ebb (Assumptions carry today's counts; the corpus has grown since the staged 195/194 measurement and the delta, not the absolute, is the finding).
The defect blocks live work. C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3 (parked branch c-payment-record-3, untouched here) cannot archive while the prose pass ships: its own spec quotes the payer phrase in the sentence that explains the pattern, and the moment that spec enters .ngrace/changes/archive/ the pass mints payments for every F-token in that sentence that no row pays — F21 among them, the token the bundle explicitly refuses. Reproduced end to end on a throwaway fixture at 49b4ebb for this spec (Assumptions item 5).

Goals.Goal: A parser-derived source-span capability in the shared XML adapter. src/artifact/xml.ts (M-GRAMMAR) gains an exported capability that, given the original XML text and its parseGraceXmlArtifact tree, returns each element's open-tag byte range and close-tag byte range, computed by pairing the parser's document-order elements with a bounded open-tag scan of the source (open-tag pattern of the form <Tag\b[^>]*>, quote-aware; self-closing elements carry an open range only). The pairing is verified against the parser at construction — element counts must agree per tag and every parsed attribute must be found inside its element's open-tag bytes — and any disagreement is a loud error, never a silent fallback to matching. Feasibility was measured, not assumed: a prototype pairing scan agrees with the parser on all six container files of the real record (213, 58, 61, 5, 12 and 36 elements respectively) and on the index's 337 self-closing Entry elements read through the self-closing branch. No reserialization exists anywhere in this bundle: the adapter's parse output, the GraceXmlNode tree, and every existing consumer are unchanged; the capability is additive.

Reads convert to the parsed tree, before writes convert, so that every write is positioned by the parser rather than by a pattern. In scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts: elementSpans callers take parser nodes with span-map offsets; attrOf becomes node.attributes, which binds attribute reads to the open tag by construction (a parser cannot read an attribute from prose); the checkStatusFile extractElements/parseAttrs path reads parsed attributes (killing the observed false status-file-mismatch class on single-quoted legal XML); readRootSnapshot, checkRulingsProvenance and checkCeilingValue read root attributes from the parsed root instead of matching the root open tag; the fenced-metadata scan's outsideBody text replacement becomes a parser walk — any text node outside a Body element that contains a fence fails; the dead childInner and childOpenAttrs helpers are deleted. The eligibility scan in validateRecordRetirement is already parser-based (walkNodes) and stays.

Writes convert to byte-preserving splices positioned by parser-derived spans. All seven document mutations keep their splice mechanics and change only their positioning: withStatusRetired rewrites the status attribute inside the open-tag range the span map located; withPaidBy inserts the PaidBy line immediately after the open tag's closing angle bracket; setEntryLayer locates the Entry element by parsed id and rewrites the layer attribute inside that open-tag range; withRootSnapshot rewrites the root's attributes within the root open-tag range; removeSpans removes exactly the parser-derived spans; appendElements inserts before the root close-tag offset instead of a lastIndexOf search. Byte preservation is a hard requirement and is tested as one: on a fixture move, every file the converted engine writes must be byte-identical to the file the shipped engine writes for the same fixture state — the diff stability, prose bytes and entity forms that citations depend on may not move.

The minimal shape check ships with the span capability, because span pairing is well defined only under it: for each of the seven record files the validator errors (code prefix record-shape-) when the root element is not the expected genre root, when a Finding, Decision, Row or Entry element appears anywhere except as a direct child of the root, or when any of those elements has a same-tag descendant. This is F207's load-bearing minimum, not the full schema: required children, depth limits beyond same-tag non-nesting, and allowed-children sets beyond what existing checks already enforce stay F207's later scope. The shape check runs on the parser tree and cannot be satisfied by the regex path.

Payment is declared structurally, not sniffed from prose. The archived-spec sentence pass in derivePayerMap — the loop that flattens each archived spec.xml, splits it into sentences, and pays every F-token in any sentence matching the payer-phrase pattern — is removed. After this bundle, the payer map is derived from exactly two declared routes, both already structural: a registry row whose name is an archive directory, via its Pays element; and that row's status text closing clause via the existing Closed-with reader. Measured consequences at 49b4ebb (Assumptions item 6): every one of the seven tokens the nine minting sentences name — F161, F130, F149, F150, F152, F43, F147 — is retired and carries a stored PaidBy stamp; five of the seven also have a row route in registry-retired.xml; F152 and F43 are prose-only routes whose stamps are stored on the retired elements and are never re-derived, because the eligibility check reads derived or stored and only live elements are ever re-examined. Removing the pass therefore un-pays nothing and un-retires nothing, and no live finding's eligibility depends on the pass today (the real record validates green at 49b4ebb).

The two probes are inherited as permanent tests, not as this bundle's one-off evidence. In scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts (fixture-based, isolated temporary roots, driving the real script by spawnSync, the shipped shape): the false-payment probe — a record fixture into which an archived spec quoting the payer phrase has been copied must leave the finding that spec refuses to pay live and eligible by no prose route, while a fixture without the copied spec stays green, so the test discriminates in both directions; and the equivalence-class probe — one live element's open tag rewritten three ways (single-quoted attributes, spaces around the equals sign, attributes reordered), each valid XML parsing identically, must give the same validate verdict and the same retire move-set as the unmodified tag. Both probes are reproduced failing against the shipped engine before the fix, in the plan's baseline, so the tests are proven to discriminate (Assumptions items 5 and 7 record the reproductions).

Constraints.Constraint: Ceremony tier T1 (module change): one script, one shared parser module, their tests; single package. Gates still run. Roadmap RM-GOVERNED-PATH. Binding live rulings: D28.1 (eligibility is the enforcement, the ceiling the backstop — this bundle changes how the payer map is derived and how spans are found, not the enforcement shape), D11 (no deferral without dependency or conflict — the deferrals below name theirs), D27 (nothing here is approved unread; the spec decides the design). Staged findings F206, F207, F208 and F209 are this bundle's findings and are cited from .ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md because the D30 window is closed to record writes; this bundle writes no record file and stages nothing into it.

Explicitly overturning part of C-RECORD-RETIREMENT's finding-eligibility Constraint, which established the initial payer population as the registry Pays column plus archived spec sentences calling an entry by the payer phrase, guarded by "mere mention of an F-id in an archived spec is not payment". The overturning answers the original argument: the guard was a judgement the engine cannot make, because a quotation of the phrase and a declaration of payment are byte-identical to a sentence scanner — C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3's spec demonstrates the collision, and F208 records the false payment it mints. The intent behind the guard (payment must be declared, not merely mentioned) is preserved and strengthened by moving declaration into the structure built for it: the registry row, whose route C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2 already called the only route and whose NonGoal ruled that archived specs are never edited to carry the phrase. The prose pass's remaining coverage is measured at zero live findings (Assumptions item 6); its false-positive cost is measured and reproduced (item 5).

F136 anchors — files this spec forces into write scope, each with its LINKS state, listed here once and not repeated as a second module list anywhere: src/artifact/xml.ts (LINKS: M-GRAMMAR) and src/artifact/xml.test.ts (no contract header; test surface of the same module); scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts and scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts (no LINKS header; scripts/ is in .ngrace-lint.json ignoredDirs; M-RELEASE-AUTOMATION is not in .ngrace/graph and its adoption remains deferred to a later C-*); this bundle's own artifacts under .ngrace/changes/active/C-RECORD-PARSE/. The module enumeration for this bundle is exactly: M-GRAMMAR (via src/artifact/xml.ts's LINKS header). No other graph module is written; do not mint a synthetic module for the scripts/ files.

Byte preservation and no ceiling arithmetic. The engine's outputs on unchanged inputs are byte-identical before and after this bundle: a --retire over the real record at 49b4ebb with nothing eligible reports moved 0 and leaves all seven record files byte-identical, and a fixture move produces byte-identical files to the shipped engine's on the same fixture state. No persisted ceiling, base or headroom value changes; persistSnapshot, the ceiling formulas and the newlineCount inputs to them are untouched (the volume metric is F206's charter, deferred below). The record files themselves are read, never written, by this bundle: no task edits docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/*, no record file is registered in CONTEXT_ARTIFACTS, and every test runs on isolated temporary fixtures in the shape scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts already uses.

Escape markup as character data in every artifact this bundle writes: tags and angle-bracketed forms appear as <Finding>, <Entry /> and <Body>-style character data, never paraphrased away to keep a document well-formed (F43). Markup-byte assertions belong in TypeScript tests, and this bundle's byte criteria are commands and tests, not prose comparisons.

Evidence hygiene, settled lessons. Every diff-based criterion scopes to exactly the paths its prose names and names the baseline it can fail against, in prose and in command alike: a base-less git diff --exit-code over paths compares the working tree to the index and passes unconditionally once the bundle's work is committed, which the close guarantees — so a diff criterion that names no commit cannot fail, and three criteria in this spec's first draft had that shape; measured on a scratch clone, committed drift over record paths passes the base-less form and fails the base-commit form (Assumptions). A byte diff answers a byte question only. It is the right instrument for a criterion whose meaning is byte-level — these files were not modified; the engine's output bytes are the promise — and the wrong instrument for document sameness, which a reformatted-but-equivalent file defeats: two bytes larger, diff exit 1, parsed trees identical (measured). Where a criterion means content, this spec answers it with the parsed validators and the shape check, never with a diff. The same base-less shape exists in one archived predecessor, C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR's AC-NO-ARCHIVE-WRITE and AC-DOCS-EXAMPLES, whose prose says pre-change tree and whose commands name no commit; this spec does not repeat it. Any pathspec covering .ngrace/changes/archive/ excludes this bundle's own directory (F188) and is probed in the post-close state (F196): after the close, this bundle's own archived spec must not be eligible to mint by any route — the prose pass is gone by then, which is what the probe asserts. Every task Verification command the later plan records exits 0 as written at recording time (F184). Task Verification and TargetAssertions contain no current-mode lint of this project root (F171); current-mode lint appears only as post-archive AC-CLOSE-LINT. bun test green is a precondition, never the evidence — the discriminating probes above are the evidence. Test measurements of the real repository carry explicit generous timeouts where the plan spawns processes (F185). Counts in this spec expire (F123); each carries its rule, command and commit, and the plan re-measures at its own base.

Editing any record file, the parked branch c-payment-record-3, or C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3's artifacts. Owner: that bundle and the authority's own acts. This bundle removes the trap its close would spring; it does not perform, preview or simulate that close.

Changing the token readers over prose fields: F_TOKEN_RE over registry Pays cells, the Closed-with clause reader, token extraction from finding bodies, and the markdown-table readers. These match prose, not XML structure, and are text processing by nature. Owner: unchanged; no user-visible surface.
README.md and examples/ unchanged; no user-visible CLI token, config key, ngrace command, lint rule or exit-code surface changes in this bundle. Owner: unchanged; no user-visible surface.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-FALSE-PAYMENT-PROBE:
The false-payment probe, both directions, on isolated fixtures built from the real record files at the plan's base commit. With the converted engine: a fixture record containing an archived spec that quotes the payer phrase — the parked bundle's spec read via git show, never checked out — leaves every finding that spec refuses to pay live, validates with no finding-eligible error attributable to a spec sentence, and the same fixture without the copied spec also validates green, so the test discriminates. Failure: any token becomes eligible because a sentence matched a pattern.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-EQUIVALENCE-CLASS:
The equivalence-class probe, all three variants. For a fixture where one live element is eligible via a registry row, rewriting that element's open tag as single-quoted attributes, as spaces around the equals signs, or with attributes reordered — each valid XML parsing identically — must yield the same validate findings and the same retire move-set as the unmodified tag (element moved to the retired sibling, stamped, index layer flipped, moved count unchanged). The shipped engine fails this today on the first two variants (element left live, moved count one low, status-file-mismatch on perfectly parsed XML), which is the baseline reproduction.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-BYTE-PRESERVING:
Byte preservation, both directions. This criterion asks a byte question and answers it with byte comparison, because byte identity is the promise itself — no reserialization, no re-indentation, no entity rewrite — not a proxy for document sameness; it therefore also forbids repairing the formatting drift the shipped engine causes as a side effect of conversion (F204's three re-indented lines are pinned as shipped output), so a later failure here is the criterion working, not a regression to be fixed. Part one: a fixture move under the converted engine writes files byte-identical to the shipped engine's output on the same fixture state (golden comparison captured in the plan's baseline before any conversion lands; the test compares read bytes). Part two: a --retire over the real record when nothing is eligible reports moved 0 and leaves all seven record files byte-identical to this spec's base commit 49b4ebb7c6627601ca77ca384f7b6e205d1f65ed — a baseline the command can fail against, demonstrated: the same command exits 1 against committed drift under those paths, while the base-less form exits 0 in that state (Assumptions). Failure: any reserialization, re-indentation, entity rewrite or reordered attribute in any written file.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts git diff --exit-code 49b4ebb7c6627601ca77ca384f7b6e205d1f65ed -- docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/findings.xml docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/findings-retired.xml docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/rulings.xml docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/rulings-retired.xml docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/registry.xml docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/registry-retired.xml docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.xml
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SHAPE-CHECK:
The shape check refuses, with a record-shape- error and exit 1: a fixture whose record contains a same-tag nested element, a genre element that is not a direct child of its root, or a wrong root element — each case on its own fixture, each valid XML that today's checks accept. The clean fixture record validates green, so the check discriminates. Failure: a malformed-shape fixture exits 0, or a clean fixture exits non-zero.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-NO-PROSE-MINT:
derivePayerMap no longer reads archived spec files: over the real archive at the plan's base commit its returned map contains no entry whose only route was a spec sentence — F152 and F43 drop out of the derived map, and the map for every other token is unchanged (rows still mint; F161, F130, F149, F150 and F147 keep their row routes). The retired elements' stored PaidBy stamps are untouched by the change and the real record still validates green after conversion. Failure: any archived spec.xml file is read by the payer derivation, or a retired element's stamp is rewritten.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-PARSER-CAPABILITY:
The span capability in src/artifact/xml.ts is verified against its own suite: for synthetic and real-record documents, open and close byte ranges are correct against known offsets, self-closing elements carry open ranges only, pairing disagreements with the parsed tree raise the documented loud error instead of returning spans, and parsed attributes are located inside their element's open-tag bytes. Failure: any span that disagrees with the source bytes it names.
bun test src/artifact/xml.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-RECORD-UNTOUCHED:
This criterion asks a byte question — that these files were not modified by this bundle, any change counting, formatting included — and a byte diff against a named baseline is the instrument that answers it; a reformatted-but-equivalent file would still be a modification, so parsed-tree sameness is not the question here and is not the test. No record file and no archived bundle is modified by this bundle's execution, measured against this spec's base commit 49b4ebb7c6627601ca77ca384f7b6e205d1f65ed. The command sees tracked edits and deletions only (F174), excludes this bundle's own later archive arrival (F188), is probed in the post-close state (F196), and can fail: it exits 1 against committed drift under those paths, where the base-less form passes (Assumptions). Failure: any path under the record directory or the archive differs from the base commit.
git diff --exit-code 49b4ebb7c6627601ca77ca384f7b6e205d1f65ed -- docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/ .ngrace/changes/archive/ ':(exclude).ngrace/changes/archive/C-RECORD-PARSE'
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-DOCS-EXAMPLES:
README.md, examples/, CLAUDE.md, docs/plans/README.md, skills/ngrace/, plugins/ngrace/skills/ngrace/, package.json and bun.lock are byte-identical to this spec's base commit 49b4ebb7c6627601ca77ca384f7b6e205d1f65ed. This is a byte question — these files were not modified by this bundle, any change counting — so the byte diff against the named baseline is the instrument, and it can fail: it exits 1 against committed drift under those paths, where the base-less form passes (Assumptions). Prose and command name the same pathset and the same baseline commit.

Post-archive lint 0/0. This is the only place current-mode lint of this root appears (F171).
